cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate is a StandardDeviationIndicator with barCount=3; getValue(2) equals standard deviation of the first three values of the underlying series
cases.description: Normal case: create a NumericIndicator from a simple BarSeries (e.g., close prices 1, 2, 3, 4). Calling stddev(3) should wrap a StandardDeviationIndicator that computes the standard deviation over the last 3 bars. Verify that the returned object is a NumericIndicator and that its delegate is an instance of StandardDeviationIndicator. Also verify the computed value matches the manually‑calculated standard deviation.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown with message containing "barCount must be > 0"
cases.description: Edge case: passing a barCount of 0 should cause the StandardDeviationIndicator constructor to reject the argument and the stddev method to propagate the IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown with message containing "barCount must be > 0"
cases.description: Edge case: passing a negative barCount should also trigger an IllegalArgumentException from the underlying StandardDeviationIndicator.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate returns NaN (Num.NaN) for any index because the underlying series contains fewer than 10 bars
cases.description: Boundary case: request a standard deviation over more bars than exist in the series. The StandardDeviationIndicator returns Num.NaN for indices where the window is incomplete. Verify that the wrapped NumericIndicator propagates this NaN value.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate returns Num.ZERO for any index because the standard deviation of a single value is 0
cases.description: Edge case: barCount = 1. For any index the StandardDeviationIndicator should compute a variance of 0, therefore the wrapped NumericIndicator must return Num.ZERO. Verify with a series of arbitrary values (e.g., 10, 20, 30).

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate returns the correct standard deviation of the whole series (indices 0‑3) and Num.NaN for any index < 3 (none in this case)
cases.description: Boundary case: barCount equals the exact number of bars in the series. Use a series with known close prices (e.g., 2, 4, 6, 8). The expected standard deviation is sqrt(((2‑5)²+(4‑5)²+(6‑5)²+(8‑5)²)/4) = 2.236... Verify that getValue(3) matches this value.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator returns Num.NaN for index 0 and the correct standard deviation for index 1 (and later indices)
cases.description: Check unstable‑bars handling: with barCount = 2 the StandardDeviationIndicator is unstable for the first (barCount‑1) = 1 bar. For a series 1, 5, 9 verify that getValue(0) is NaN and getValue(1) equals sqrt(((1‑3)²+(5‑3)²)/2) = 2.828...

cases.expected: NumericIndicator returns the correct standard deviation for index 4 (the first complete window) and NaN for indices 0‑3
cases.description: Series length exactly matches barCount. Use a series of five values (e.g., 3, 3, 3, 3, 7). The first four windows are incomplete → NaN. At index 4 the window contains [3,3,3,3,7]; expected stddev = sqrt(((3‑3.8)²*4+(7‑3.8)²)/5) ≈ 1.720.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator returns Num.ZERO for index 2 because the first three values are identical, and correct non‑zero stddev for later windows
cases.description: Zero‑variance window: series 5,5,5,6,7. For barCount 3, the window ending at index 2 is [5,5,5] → stddev 0. Verify getValue(2) == Num.ZERO, while getValue(3) and getValue(4) produce the expected non‑zero values.

Confirm that the wrapper propagates the unstable‑bars information from the underlying StandardDeviationIndicator. After creating stddev(3) on any series, calling getUnstableBars() on the resulting NumericIndicator should equal 2.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator.delegate() is an instance of StandardDeviationIndicator
cases.description: Verify the internal delegate type: the stddev method must wrap the StandardDeviationIndicator. After calling stddev(3), the returned NumericIndicator’s delegate() should be instanceof StandardDeviationIndicator.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown when constructing StandardDeviationIndicator because the NumericIndicator was created with a null delegate
cases.description: Create a NumericIndicator via NumericIndicator.of(null). Calling stddev(3) should propagate a NullPointerException from the StandardDeviationIndicator constructor, which expects a non‑null delegate.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because the underlying delegate's getBarSeries() returns null
cases.description: Implement a custom Indicator<Num> that returns null for getBarSeries() (while providing valid getValue and getUnstableBars). Wrap it with NumericIndicator.of(customIndicator) and invoke stddev(3). The StandardDeviationIndicator will attempt to access the series and throw a NullPointerException.
